sub.name: Continuity and responsiveness

sub.limitation: material: Healer turns 3 and 6 ignore prior objections; near-monologue.

sub.name: Development of ideas
sub.example: Turn 5 adds inflamed-baseline confound; turn 7 builds a 7-day wait on it.
sub.limitation: material: turn 6 restates turn 3, adding nothing new.

sub.name: Exploration of central tensions
sub.example: Turn 9 frames single ingredient versus cumulative change.
sub.limitation: material: irritant vs allergic reaction, strong actives, when to see a doctor never raised.

sub.name: Integration of perspectives
sub.example: Turn 7: Reductionist absorbs Minimalist's recovery pause into the protocol.
sub.limitation: material: Healer's stress view never integrated or tested by others.

criteria.name: Quality of disagreement, trust and grounding

sub.name: Faithful engagement
sub.example: Turn 5 restates Reductionist's unsolved-question concern accurately.
sub.limitation: material: turn 2 opposes testing though turn 1 already stops all three products.

sub.name: Substance of challenges
sub.example: Turn 5 names the clean-baseline assumption and the misread it causes; turn 7 answers.
sub.limitation: material: turn 6 objection is unspecific and unanswered by anyone.

sub.name: Accuracy and support
sub.example: No quotation marks; all pd false; books exist.
sub.limitation: material: turns 3, 6 stretch van der Kolk to skin stinging; section E inference unsupported.

sub.name: Calibration and transparency
sub.example: Turns hedge with 'might' rather than asserting diagnoses.
sub.limitation: material: section E says 'likely reacting to a specific chemical' from a 24-hour stop.

sub.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
sub.example: Turn 7: Reductionist explicitly drops immediate testing.
sub.limitation: material: Healer never answers turn 4's unsolved-culprit objection.

sub.name: Identification of the actual concern
sub.example: Section D separates finding the culprit from ending discomfort.
sub.limitation: material: severity and safety of the reaction never treated as part of the concern.

sub.name: Meaningful use of personal context
sub.example: Turn 1 uses three products started together to set isolation.
sub.limitation: material: product types or ingredients never used to shape the reasoning.

sub.name: Fit with goals and values
sub.example: Turn 8 weighs lost skincare progress against clarity.
sub.limitation: minor: user's skincare goals assumed, not identified.

sub.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
sub.example: Turn 5 flags reintroducing on inflamed skin as risky.
sub.limitation: material: no warning signs (swelling, eyes, hives) or medical threshold.

sub.name: Responsiveness to information
sub.example: Turn 8 asks whether one product feels harshest.
sub.limitation: material: never asks which products, actives like retinoids or acids, or severity.

sub.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
sub.example: Section D offers culprit-finding versus quick relief as alternatives with a question.
sub.limitation: material: appears only in summary; debate turns never explore it.

sub.name: Examination of assumptions
sub.example: Turn 9 questions the assumption that one ingredient is to blame.
sub.limitation: material: assumption that products caused it at all, or need for all three, unexamined.

sub.name: Clarification of values and priorities
sub.example: Turn 8: clarity versus routine progress.
sub.limitation: material: conflict raised once, never weighed by other minds.

sub.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
sub.example: Turn 3 notes being overwhelmed by changes.
sub.limitation: material: turn 3 casts stinging as skin reflecting stress, edging toward pathologising.

sub.name: Agency and reflective ownership
sub.example: Section E gives branches the user can choose among.
sub.limitation: material: few distinctions the user could refine; mostly a protocol handed down.

sub.name: Definition of the decision and options
sub.example: Turns 1, 2, 7: stop all, full pause, staged reintroduction.
sub.limitation: material: patch testing, keeping one product, or seeing a dermatologist never offered.

sub.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
sub.example: Turn 8 names lost time as cost of the 7-day wait.
sub.limitation: material: cost of the multi-week protocol never totalled or compared.

sub.name: Identification of decisive conditions
sub.example: Section E: sting after 48 hours of water favours recovery.
sub.limitation: material: 7 and 3 day figures not drawn from user facts; branch logic doubtful.

sub.name: Treatment of uncertainty
sub.example: Turn 9 names the unresolved cause question.
sub.limitation: material: allergy versus irritation, the consequential unknown, never separated.

sub.name: Proportionate next steps
sub.example: Section E: log reintroductions one product every 3 days.
sub.limitation: material: no escalation step if symptoms worsen.

sub.name: Accessible language
sub.example: Turn 7 states plain days and steps.
sub.limitation: minor: turn 6 'cumulative pressure of routines' is vague.

sub.name: Traceable arguments and references
sub.example: Turns 4 and 5 name the speaker they answer.
sub.limitation: minor: turn 6 'If you feel' target ambiguous; turn 3 answers unnamed testing.

sub.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
sub.example: Nine turns, each within 25 to 65 words.
sub.limitation: minor: Healer's turns stall pace at 3 and 6.

sub.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
sub.example: Reductionist's isolation stance is distinct.
sub.limitation: material: Minimalist and Healer both argue a pause; all speak in identical 'you might' hedges.

sub.name: Economy and sustained attention
sub.example: Section E condenses the debate into three branches.
sub.limitation: material: turn 6 repeats turn 3's overwhelm point.

sub.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
sub.example: Turn 4: culprit may stay unknown if you just quit.
sub.limitation: material: tension low; turns 1 and 2 largely agree on stopping.

sub.name: Surprise and reversals
sub.example: Turn 7: Reductionist drops immediate testing.
sub.limitation: material: turn 7 reversal names no turn or argument that changed his mind.

sub.name: Personality and expressive voice
sub.example: Healer's body-signal framing gives slight colour.
sub.limitation: material: all three minds flat, uniformly hedged.

sub.name: Memorable delivery
sub.example: Turn 9's 48-hour water test is concrete.
sub.limitation: material: no analogy, vivid example or sharp line anywhere.

sub.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
sub.example: Turn 9 sets up an unresolved test.
sub.limitation: material: uniform low intensity across all nine turns.

strengths: Turn 5's inflamed-baseline confound is a real mid-debate distinction that turn 7 uses.
Section E gives observable conditions (48-hour water test) tied to options.
Section D poses culprit versus quick relief as a question the user can answer.
weaknesses: Never asks which products or actives, nor gives warning signs for seeing a doctor.
Healer (turns 3, 6) misapplies trauma framing to skin stinging and repeats itself.
Turn 7 reversal unexplained; all three voices flat and alike in hedging.
editorNotes: Require one turn to ask for the consequential missing facts (product names, actives, severity) with what each answer implies.
Require minds whose sources actually fit the domain; forbid stretching a book to an unrelated mechanism.
Require any change of position to name the earlier turn and argument that caused it.
For health situations, require a safety threshold branch (when to stop and see a professional).
